intro: CAT is a 120-minute computer-based test in three time-locked sections of 40 minutes each, in fixed order: VARC, DILR and QA. Section names below follow this site's labels: english is VARC, reasoning is DILR and quant is QA.
note: IIMs do not publish an official syllabus; the topic lists below are the conventional scope based on past papers, and the official announcement on iimcat.ac.in gives only the exam frame. Marking: +3 per correct answer, minus 1 per wrong MCQ, and no negative marking for TITA (Type In The Answer) questions, with an on-screen calculator provided. Question counts are never pre-announced; the CAT 2025 paper had 24 questions in VARC, 22 in DILR and 22 in QA.

sections.name: VARC (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)
topics: Reading comprehension (long passages on philosophy, economics, science, history and culture)
sections.tip: Reading comprehension dominates (four passages of four questions each plus eight verbal ability items in CAT 2025), so the real skill is dense reading under time, not grammar rules.

sections.name: DILR (Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning)
sections.tip: DILR comes as about five sets of 4 to 5 questions each (22 questions in CAT 2025), mixing data sets with puzzle sets; set selection, not solving everything, is the tested skill.

sections.name: QA (Quantitative Ability)
topics: Algebra: equations, inequalities, functions and graphs
sections.tip: Arithmetic carries the largest share in recent CAT papers, followed by algebra and geometry; the level is roughly Class 10 mathematics, but framed in long, layered word problems (22 questions in CAT 2025).
